title: Angular Introduction
summary: Meet Angular, a set of tools for building web apps. Learn how a small page part can show a name and count button clicks.
introduction: Think of a web page as a set of building blocks. One block shows a name. Another block holds a button. Angular helps you make these blocks and keep their values up to date. Each block is called a component.
learningObjectives: Explain what an Angular component is
Show a name in a heading
Use a signal to keep a changing score

rows: One part of a page, like a score card.
The HTML that says what a component shows.
A value Angular watches for changes.

blocks.title: Where to run the examples
blocks.text: Read the [setup lesson](/tutorials/angular/setup-cli) to use Angular on your computer. These examples are shown here for reading; they do not run in this site playground.
The template holds a heading. The selector gives this part its HTML name. Add Greeting to the parent component imports, then put <app-greeting /> in its template.

blocks.title: greeting.ts

blocks.text: Put a value in the page
The name field stores text. The two curly brackets place that text inside the heading. This keeps the value separate from the page layout.

blocks.title: greeting.ts

blocks.text: A signal stores the score. score() reads it. A click calls add(), which adds one. Use <app-score /> in a parent that imports Score.

blocks.title: score.ts
What you should see
blocks.content:
At the start: Score: 0
After one click: Score: 1

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: Use a modern Angular project for these examples. AngularJS is an older, different tool. The two use different code.

blocks.title: Try one small change
blocks.text: In the first example, change Asha to your name. In the last example, click three times and check the score.
